findings.evidence:
Step 6 has a 13-line Mermaid flowchart example (subgraph, node shapes, edge labels). The model already knows flowchart syntax. The only new part is the label convention "Name
[Container: Tech]".
findings.fix:
Shrink the example to two lines that show only the convention, for example `api["Order API
[Container: Node.js]"]` and `customer -->|"Places orders
HTTPS"| api`. Keep the downgrade statement.

findings.evidence: Audience rows such as "| Executives | Context only |" and "| Product managers | Context + Container |" repeat the standard C4 audience guidance the model already knows.
findings.fix: Merge the table into one default, "Context + Container unless the audience or request narrows it". Keep only the rows that are not obvious: DevOps maps to Container + Deployment, and a flow maps to Dynamic.

findings.evidence: The evidence-to-element table assumes each source of evidence is unambiguous. It has no procedure for evidence that conflicts, for example compose and k8s that disagree, or one image run as several compose services with different `command:` values.
findings.fix: Add two rows. First: "Compose services that share one image or build but have different `command:` values are separate containers." Second: "When compose and production manifests disagree, model the production manifest and record the conflict as Inferred in the evidence table."

findings.evidence: Most should-trigger queries are terse and formal, such as "Make C4 context and container diagrams for our customer portal and its services." None has file paths, backstory, casual phrasing or typos, and most name C4 or architecture outright.
findings.fix: Rewrite 4-5 positives as realistic, indirect requests. Example: "new hire starts monday, can u give them a picture of how web/api/worker in ~/code/shop talk to postgres and stripe? compose file is in the root".

findings.evidence: "Represents the known user and backend at an appropriate abstraction" cannot be checked objectively.
findings.fix: Replace it with a checkable assertion: "Contains a C4Context with one Person for users and one System for the backend, and no Container, ContainerDb or Deployment_Node elements."

findings.evidence: The row "| Architects or developers | Context + Container, plus Component for the container they ask about |" does not say what to do when no container is named, or when several rows match. Eval 1 has "product and engineering" and matches two rows. Following that branch leaves it unclear whether to produce a Component view.
findings.fix: Add this after the table: "When several audiences match, produce the union of their views. When developers are the audience but no container is named, produce Context + Container only and offer a Component view for the container with the most distinct responsibilities."
